summary: A list of records beside the one selected — people, tickets, messages, files. Arrow down the list and the detail beside it follows, without anything to open or close; the selection is in the address.
useWhen: the user works down a list reading each item in turn — members, an inbox, a queue of tickets — and wants the next without going back
each record is read or lightly acted on in its detail, not a task that must be finished before anything else
a row has a name and a line or two, not columns to compare down

useInstead.when: the rows have columns compared down — status, owner, duration side by side
useInstead.use: the DataTable pattern, whose SidePanel opens from a per-row Details button
useInstead.why: a Table's rows hold links and buttons of their own, so its selection cannot follow focus; the detail opens on a press there, and stays open while the next is opened

useInstead.when: the record is the whole of what the user came for — minutes in it, sections, tabs, a history
useInstead.use: a page of its own, linked from the list
useInstead.why: a side view of a third of the width is a preview; a record worked in needs the whole page and its own address

useInstead.when: the detail is a form that must be saved or cancelled
useInstead.why: a detail that changes as focus moves would throw away what was typed the moment the user arrows to the next row

structure: A PageHeader naming the collection — "Members" — then, over the list only, a SearchField (size sm, an `aria-label` naming what it searches) when the list is long enough to need one.
A SidePanelLayout: the List first, the SidePanel second — reading order is DOM order, and the detail is the detail of the list before it.

Each row: `label` the record's name, `description` the line that tells two alike apart (an email, a subject), `leading` an Avatar or Icon (hidden from assistive technology, so it repeats nothing the label lacks), `meta` a Badge for one fact worth scanning for ("Admin"). Nothing interactive in the row: the row is the control.

At 768px and wider, `selectionMode="single"`: the selection follows focus, so tabbing in selects the first row and each ↓ selects the next. The SidePanel is open while a row is selected, with `autoFocus={false}` — it opened because of where focus already is, and focus stays on the row. Tab goes on into the panel, next in the DOM; Escape there closes it and returns focus to the row. Enter or a double click (`onAction`) moves focus to the panel's title, for the user who wants to read on.

Below 768px, where the SidePanel opens as a modal Drawer, no selection mode: a row opens on a press (`onAction`), never on arrival, or tabbing into the list would open a dialog. Closing the Drawer returns focus to the row.

The selection is in the address — `#/members/usr_ada`, `/members/usr_ada` — so a link, a reload and a shared URL open the same record. Replace the history entry as the selection moves, never push: with a push, every row arrowed past is a Back press, and Back no longer leaves the page. The list and the address are one page: moving the selection must not mount the page again.

The panel's title is the record's name and its description one fact about it ("Workspace admin"). What the list already fetched shows at once — a DescriptionList, IDs and addresses with an icon-only CopyButton named for what it copies ("Copy email"). Anything that needs its own request loads inside the panel, below them.
A selected row the search hides: the panel closes with it, and opens again when the row comes back. Detail of a row the user can no longer see is a lie about the list.

An address whose ID matches nothing: the list as usual, and the panel open with an EmptyState — `reason="no-results"`, `size="panel"` — saying so ("There is no member with this ID") and a Button that clears the selection. Not a full-page 404: the page exists; one record in it does not.

loading.must: The list: Skeleton rows in its place, `aria-busy` on their container and a status saying what is loading. The detail's own request: a Skeleton inside the panel, under the facts the list already had — never the whole panel blanked.
loading.why: blanking the panel on each ↓ while the next record loads makes arrowing down the list a flicker, and hides what was already known
loading.a11y: the panel's loading is a status inside it, not a live announcement per row — the row's name is already being read as the selection moves

empty.must: No records: an EmptyState in the list's place, `size="page"`, and no panel. A search that matches nothing: the List's `renderEmptyState` saying what was searched for ("No one matches “zzz”."), the SearchField still there to change it.
empty.why: an empty grid is announced as "0 rows" and nothing else; the user must be told whether the collection is empty or their search is

error.must: The list failing is the page failing: the FullPageError pattern. The detail's own request failing: an Alert inside the panel naming what is missing, with Try again, while the list and the facts it had stay.
error.why: one record's missing part is not a reason to take away the list, or the rest of the record
error.a11y: the panel's Alert takes `role="alert"` from its intent — do not add your own

requires: the List's `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, naming the collection

`autoFocus={false}` on the SidePanel beside a single-selection List: with it on, tabbing into the list selects the first row, opens the panel and takes focus out of the list before a key has been pressed
rows that open on a press, not on focus, where the panel is a Drawer: a modal dialog must not open because focus arrived somewhere
notes: Selection following focus is the listbox convention for a selection that is not disruptive, and a panel updating beside the list is not: focus stays put, and the row's name — read as it is selected — says which record the panel shows.
The panel is a named region, so a screen reader user can reach it by landmark as well as by Tab.

antiPatterns.dont: a SidePanel that takes focus on open beside a List whose selection follows focus
antiPatterns.why: Tab into the list selects the first row, the panel opens and takes focus, and the list can never be walked

antiPatterns.dont: pushing a history entry for each selection
antiPatterns.why: arrowing down ten rows makes Back take ten presses to leave the page

antiPatterns.dont: a panel that opens as soon as a row is focused, on a phone
antiPatterns.do: no selection mode below 768px, and `onAction` opening the row
antiPatterns.why: there the panel is a modal Drawer: arriving in the list would open a dialog and trap the user in it

antiPatterns.dont: a full-page 404 for an ID that matches no record in a list that loaded
antiPatterns.do: the list, and the panel saying there is no such record
antiPatterns.why: the page is there; one record is not, and the rest of the list is the way forward

antiPatterns.dont: buttons or links inside the rows
antiPatterns.why: a row that is also a selection target and holds its own controls cannot follow focus: → into a row's button would change nothing the panel shows, and the user loses track of which is which
